name: OutlierDetectionOptions
description: Failure counting that ejects an endpoint for a while, and an optional application-defined health check. The library does not know what healthy means. It counts classified failures, ejects an endpoint by time, and puts it back when the time is up; only isHealthy can say that an endpoint is unfit, and only the application supplies it. No timers, ejection quotas, settlement grid, or slow start are used.

name: outlierDetection
description: Wraps a strategy with consecutive-failure ejection by time. Five attributed failures eject an endpoint by default. The penalty is the minimum penalty (1s by default) times the penalty level, so successive ejections last 1s, 2s, 3s and so on; uniform positive jitter of up to 0.5 times the base is added, and the total caps at 60s. When the time is up the endpoint is selectable again; nothing probes it or decides that it has recovered. As in gRPC outlier detection (gRFC A50) a success never clears the penalty level: every ejection raises it by one and every ten seconds without one lowers it by one, evaluated when the endpoint is next used. An endpoint that accepts a connection and then drops it is therefore ejected for longer each time, as long as its failures return faster than one level decays. Every classified failure code fails by default, including NET_TIMEOUT and NET_BODY_INCOMPLETE, as Envoy's consecutive 5xx and gRPC outlier detection count timeouts and resets; isFailure replaces that rule. An attempted outcome without a code resets the streak; unattributed attempts and discarded samples leave it unchanged. The outcome of an attempt that began before an ejection, or while the endpoint was ejected, is ignored even if it arrives after the endpoint is selectable again, so late results do not eject it anew. The child receives the filtered candidates as endpoints and the unfiltered members, so ejection does not look like a membership change to it. isHealthy, when supplied, is the only health judgement and combines with ejection by AND: it can keep an endpoint out, and true cannot let an ejected endpoint in. If it rejects every endpoint that is not ejected, it is ignored for that pick. If every endpoint is ejected, the original current list is used (Finagle panic mode). Unlike Envoy and gRPC A50 there is no ejection quota. All callbacks are synchronous; no timer is created. Configuration is captured at construction. History holds at least 256 endpoints, and at least the current list, shared across endpoint lists. LRU clean or expired states are evicted first, then partial failure sequences, then the oldest protected state only if every retained endpoint is ejected. Temporary candidate exclusion does not itself erase a penalty.
